card: This pull request migrates headers presync DoS-protection parameters (commitment period and redownload buffer size) from static chainparams constants to runtime computation during node startup. Previously, maintainers were required to run an offline Python script during each release cycle to guess the release's active lifetime and commit fixed tuning parameters, creating maintenance friction and risking parameter degradation over time. The ported C++ solver also fixes a flaw in the former script's attack model where attackers were assumed unable to halt mid-batch. The offline tool is deleted, and extensive fuzz and unit tests verify the solver against known exhaustive optima. There are no dependencies.
changed_since_previous: No substantive changes to the approach or structure; commits and functionality match the previous revision.
evidence: PR description: "Less work for maintainers that need to occasionally run the current contrib/devtools/headerssync-params.py script. Less room for mistakes in that process. Automatically adapts based on time (as opposed to needing to predict the lifetime of the software)."

PR description notes the old model "actually got it (slightly) wrong by missing the fact that attackers are capable of strategically deciding to stop the attack in the middle of a batch (found by darosior)."
problem: Maintainers previously had to manually run an offline Python script during release preparation and estimate the expected operational lifetime of the release to compute static sync parameters, creating release overhead and room for human error. Additionally, the old modeling script had a flaw assuming attackers could only submit headers in rigid 2000-header batches rather than aborting strategically mid-batch.

risk.why: A flaw in the parameter calculation could degrade DoS protection against low-difficulty header spam or cause unexpected memory allocation during initial headers sync.

scope_notes: Deletes contrib/devtools/headerssync-params.py (-357 lines) and adds 50 test vectors in headerssync_tests.cpp along with two dedicated fuzz targets.
summary: Computes headers presync DoS-protection parameters (the commitment period and redownload buffer size) dynamically at node startup instead of hardcoding precomputed values in chainparams. The optimization algorithm is implemented in C++ in headerssync, calculating optimal values based on elapsed time since genesis and the minimum chainwork height. The offline parameter generator contrib/devtools/headerssync-params.py is removed, and consensus parameters are updated with minchainwork_height.
